items.title: Public Meetings to Consider Zoning Amendments
RZ007-24 6518 First Line, Fergus
notes: Mayor Watters indicated the public meeting is to present and receive public input regarding a proposed zoning by-law amendment on land within the Centre Wellington Business Park in Fergus.

He noted the purpose of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to modify the zoning regulations for the Centre Wellington Business Park – North Fergus, including changes to the permitted uses and the lot regulations.
The effect of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to implement the recommendations of the Centre Wellington Business Park Strategy.

He indicated if a person or public body would otherwise have an ability to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) but the person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision.

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body may not be added as a party to the hearing of an appeal before the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters advised if anyone wishes to be notified of the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington in respect of the proposed zoning by- law amendment, a written request must be made to the Municipal Clerk of the Township of Centre Wellington, 1 MacDonald Square, Elora, Ontario, N0B 1S0.

The Municipal Clerk advised notice was provided to prescribed persons, agencies and public bodies on or before December 19, 2024. A copy was also placed in the Wellington Advertiser on December 19, 2024.
The Municipal Clerk confirmed the requirement for giving notice was completed on December 19, 2024.
Mayor Watters asked Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development, to present the application.

Brett Salmon, Managing Director of Planning provided an overview of the proposal, including the scope of the new M2.BP zone and the new uses to be added as well as the permitted uses to be deleted. He indicated the permitted uses to be added include the following: artisan studio, communication and broadcasting establishment, emergency service facility, laboratory, and business or professional office excluding a medical clinic.

B. Salmon outlined additional lot and building regulations relief sought, including the outdoor storage area, minimum lot frontage, side, front and rear yard set backs, minimum landscaped area and buffer strip.
B. Salmon responded to questions regarding the restriction on outdoor display, rationale for excluding medical office/clinic, inclusion of shared space and/or multi-tenant units.
Mayor Watters indicated there are no delegations registered and asked if there was anyone present who wished to speak to the application.
There being none, Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and indicated the application will be considered later in the meeting. He declared the public meeting adjourned.

items.title: OFM Fire Protection Grant Transfer Payment Agreement
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Dan Wilson, CAO provided an overview of the report, indicating the Fire Chief in collaboration with staff have applied for the grant money to purchase particulate blocking hoods that will offer increased protection by blocking more than 99.8% of toxic particles absorbed into the skin from burning materials during a fire.
Fire Chief Tom Mulvey responded to a question regarding the hoods, indicating replacing the current hoods for all staff, including 66 volunteer firefighters and 4 management staff.
Councillor Wilton, having declared a conflict of interest left the room and therefore did not participate in the discussion nor did she vote on the next item.

items.title: Zoning Amendment RZ04-2024 Decision Report - 750 St David Street
notes: N., Fergus
Report from D. Maiden, Senior Development Planner

D. Maiden, Senior Development Planner provided an overview of the report, including the scope of the amendment. She noted the property currently contains a single detached bungalow and detached garage that will be removed to facilitate redevelopment. The application seeks to amend the zoning from R1C - Residential to R4 – Residential with exemptions, as outlined in the staff report. The redevelopment proposes 12, 2-bedroom purpose built rental units, with 18 parking spaces, along with secure, exterior bicycle lockers.

D. Maiden indicated concerns raised related primarily to street parking, traffic, location of a new access on Parkside Drive East, snow removal, light pollution, servicing (water pressure) and retention of trees. She noted staff are of the opinion most of the concerns raised have been adequately addressed or can be addressed through a future site plan process.
D. Maiden responded to questions regarding the location of the driveway, and the various technical studies submitted in support of the application.

Pierre Chauvin, MHBC responded to questions related to the functionality of St. David Street as an arterial road, the intention to rent the units, and the location of multi-residential and commercial uses across the street.
Colin Baker, Managing Director of Infrastructure Services noted future plans for bike lanes, traffic calming, improved signage and safety measures.

items.title: Zoning Amendment RZ07/24 Decision Report - Centre Wellington
notes: Business Park
Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development provided an overview of the report and responded to questions.

Councillor MacDonald suggested including a medical office/clinic in the permitted uses. Discussion ensued and Council directed staff to review the M2 zoning with a view to expand the permitted uses to include a medical office/clinic.

items.title: Affordable Residential Unit Development Charge Exemption
notes: Agreements
Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Dan Wilson, CAO provided an overview of the report, indicating the purpose of the report is to provide an update on a newly enacted affordable residential unit development charge exemption that is now contained in the Development Charges Act (DCA), 1997. He responded to questions regarding the affordability thresholds, and the requirement to enter into agreements before the exemption is applied.
